timelineEvents.title: Private study and first Berlin networks
timelineEvents.label: 1926–1930 · Berlin study and networks
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper builds his Berlin career through private study with Moritz Mayer-Mahr and Walther Gmeindl, early publications, and collaboration with Fritz Rotter.
timelineEvents.longDescription: After moving to Berlin, Kaper developed his professional position through private study with pianist Moritz Mayer-Mahr and composer-conductor Walther Gmeindl, while also entering the German-language song market through Fritz Rotter and early publications under the title “Dr. Kaper.” By his own account in the 1975 oral-history interview, it was the composer Jerzy Fitelberg, among the friends he found in Berlin, who urged him to study privately rather than at the Hochschule. He had come to Berlin intending to enrol at the Staatliche Akademische Hochschule für Musik, but gave up the idea of a virtuoso career before the entrance examination, and a plan to study privately with Artur Schnabel foundered on the fees. Róża Etkin, whom he knew from the Chopin school in Warsaw, sent him to Mayer-Mahr, who urged him not to abandon the piano.
